items.title: Per-machine defaults for remote windows
items.text: Each remote machine can now remember its own default working directory and shell. Open the machine chooser (⇧⌘N), click a machine's `⋯` menu → "Host Settings…", and every new window, tab, and split on that machine starts where — and in the shell — you want. Leave a field empty to keep the machine's own default.

items.title: Pick your Windows shell
items.text: On Windows hosts you can choose cmd, PowerShell, pwsh, or WSL bash (or type any shell path). Commands now run with each shell's correct convention, so PowerShell and WSL sessions launch commands correctly instead of failing with cmd.exe-style flags.

items.title: New CLI flags
items.text: `ghoztty +new-remote-window` now accepts `--working-directory=`, `--shell=`, and `--command=` to control the remote session per window; explicit flags override the machine's saved defaults.

items.title: Splits and tabs follow your settings
items.text: New tabs and splits on a remote window use the machine's default shell while still opening in the directory of the pane you split from.
